changelog: Twenty-five things the owner found by walking the new configuration app, and all of them are answered here. Four were one fault each seen from several ends. The selection highlight was cut off almost everywhere because every ring was drawn outside the thing it marks, so the bar that starts where a programme ends painted over its bottom edge - the rings are inside now, which also stops every card and list clipping them. The Save button stayed grey over real edits because dirty was a flag twenty places had to remember to set; it is measured now, against what the server last gave us, so no control can miss it and putting a value back un-marks it. Dragging a programme to another time was never built, and dragging from the shelf did reach the server - which stored a row of zero seconds, drawn as a hairline and playing for no time at all, because the page deliberately sends no length and nothing filled it in. And the two buttons on the new-channel screen that did nothing did nothing for a good reason: they minted an id with a browser call that only exists on https, so on a dashboard reached by its address on the network the click threw before it could change anything. That one also broke Create. The rest, screen by screen. A channel that runs programmes back to back is no longer one blob. Delete moves to the next airing so a run can be cleared. A series on the shelf opens into seasons and episodes to drag from. A YouTube playlist is read before it is added, on the content list and on the shelf, where it goes on as its videos rather than one tag - the plugin could always expand a playlist when a week was laid out, but nothing could ask, which is exactly what "fetching does not work" was. Blocks are a list, not a week view, asked for twice. Selecting a source now says what selecting is for. "Nothing to play yet" says whether it means the channel or the Save button. The break settings moved to Breaks, where anyone would look for them. On Look: the channel name is drawn only where a television draws it, the gallery searches the whole library instead of offering only this channel's own titles, previews show the whole picture instead of cropping it, the upload button wears an upload, and the television preview follows what the app actually does - banner first in the channel list, backdrop first behind the channel screen, both dimmed hard, with a line saying which picture it used and why. Suggestions gained a similarity cut-off that runs the whole range. The server screen offers its two typed fields as drop-downs - the YouTube client list is the resolver's own ladder, so the two cannot drift - and old builds can be cleared out in one press. The app also sizes itself to the room it is given rather than to a guessed height, which is what left a band of empty space under it and stopped the build list scrolling.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
